claim: A plural reflexive complement with a collective subject and singular verb is excluded.
evidence_summary: Smith gives the government has offered themselves as marginal. An annual report has a team that has outshone themselves.
finding: Some speakers allow the singular-verb/plural-reflexive direction more readily than its converse. The published judgments and the annual-report example document variation. They do not estimate prevalence by variety, register or period.
proposed_wording: Some speakers allow a singular verb with a collective subject and a plural reflexive complement. Acceptability varies across speakers and with the direction of the mismatch.
inference: Does singular verbal agreement block a later plural reflexive with the same collective antecedent?

evidence.source: Peter W. Smith (2017). The syntax of semantic agreement in English. Journal of Linguistics 53, 823–863.
evidence.passage: §17.2.5, p. 496. A plural reflexive complement with a collective subject and singular verb is excluded.
evidence.example: Nine speakers of varieties allowing plural collective agreement preferred has offered themselves to have offered itself. Some found the former marginal.
evidence.establishes: Supports a directional asymmetry and speaker variation. It does not establish acceptance across English varieties.

evidence.example: The handout includes the U.N. finds themselves among its collective examples.
evidence.establishes: An additional judgment in the singular-verb/plural-reflexive direction.

evidence.passage: §17.2.5, p. 496. A plural reflexive complement with a collective subject and singular verb is excluded.
evidence.example: The report uses “our multi-talented team has truly outshone themselves”. The collective subject controls singular has, while the reflexive object is plural.
evidence.establishes: An attestation of this direction of agreement mismatch in organizational prose.
